title: American put by CRR binomial tree, single contract
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T (years), r, q, sigma (decimal), steps N. DITANYAKAN: American put price, European put price, premium = American - European (currency). RUMUS: card Core 1 CRR: dt=T/N, u=e^{sigma sqrt dt}, d=1/u, p=(e^{(r-q)dt}-d)/(u-d); V=max(K-S_node, e^{-r dt}[pV_u+(1-p)V_d]); toolkit crr_price(american=True), bs_price for European. JAWAB: 1) convert percent inputs. 2) terminal payoff max(K-S_T,0) [N+1]. 3) roll back with max(continuation, intrinsic) at every node incl. t=0. 4) European by bs_price (or same tree without max). 5) premium. 6) check American >= max(European, K-S). 7) round last, write.
formulas: V = max(K - S, e^{-r dt}[p V_u + (1-p) V_d])
pitfalls: computing the European leg with a different method than the American inflates the premium by discretisation error; state which

title: American call with continuous dividend yield, per-contract CRR table
deliverables: per-contract table [M]: id, american_price, european_price, premium
frame: DIKETAHUI: [M] contracts: id, S, K, T, r, q>0, sigma; steps N. DITANYAKAN: per contract American call, European call, premium (currency) [M]. RUMUS: CRR with p=(e^{(r-q)dt}-d)/(u-d); node value max(S-K, continuation); toolkit crr_price(kind='call', american=True, q=q), bs_price(q=q). JAWAB: 1) read [M] rows, keep id dtype and order. 2) percent -> decimal per column. 3) loop contracts: tree price [M]. 4) European closed form [M]. 5) premium [M]. 6) check premium >= 0, premium grows with q, zero when q=0. 7) write table.
formulas: C_am = max(S - K, e^{-r dt}[p C_u + (1-p) C_d])
pitfalls: q enters both p and the European formula; dropping it from p overprices the call

title: American call on non-dividend stock equals European
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r>0, sigma, q=0, no cash dividends. DITANYAKAN: American call value and early exercise premium. RUMUS: Merton: C_am >= S - K e^{-rT} > S - K, so early exercise never optimal; C_am = BS call (toolkit bs_price). JAWAB: 1) confirm q=0 and no discrete dividends. 2) price European via bs_price. 3) report American = European, premium = 0 (a tree gives ~1e-4 discrepancy - report closed form unless the task demands the tree). 4) if a tree is required, report tree value and its difference to BS as discretisation error. 5) write.
pitfalls: reporting a tree-noise premium as real early exercise value

title: CRR odd/even oscillation: average of N and N+1 steps
deliverables: scalar: price_N, price_N1, price_avg; optional convergence table [K] over N
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, q, sigma, N (or list of N [K]). DITANYAKAN: American price with N, N+1 steps and their average; optional error vs reference. RUMUS: card V2(b): P_avg = (P_N + P_{N+1})/2; toolkit crr_price(steps=N) and steps=N+1. JAWAB: 1) price with N. 2) price with N+1. 3) average. 4) if reference (BAW or N=10000) given, error per N [K]. 5) check averaged error smaller and monotone. 6) write.
pitfalls: averaging N and N+2 (same parity) does not cancel the oscillation

title: Binomial Black-Scholes (BBS) smoothing with Richardson extrapolation
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, q, sigma, N. DITANYAKAN: BBS price (last step replaced by BS) and BBSR = Richardson of BBS at N and N/2. RUMUS: at step N-1 nodes continuation = BS European with tau=dt (bs_price), then max with intrinsic; roll back CRR; BBSR = 2 P_N - P_{N/2} (first-order). JAWAB: 1) build tree to N-1. 2) node values max(K-S, bs_price(S_node, K, dt)). 3) roll back with early exercise. 4) repeat with N/2. 5) Richardson. 6) compare with plain CRR. 7) write.
pitfalls: card Core 6 4:1 weights are for 2nd-order PDE schemes; trees converge O(1/N) so weights are 2:1

title: Boyle trinomial tree for American put
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, q, sigma, N. DITANYAKAN: American put price by trinomial lattice (and European, premium). RUMUS: card Core 1 Boyle: b=r-q, u=e^{sigma sqrt(2dt)}, pu=((e^{b dt/2}-e^{-sigma sqrt(dt/2)})/(e^{sigma sqrt(dt/2)}-e^{-sigma sqrt(dt/2)}))^2, pd=((e^{sigma sqrt(dt/2)}-e^{b dt/2})/(same))^2, pm=1-pu-pd. JAWAB: 1) nodes S u^j, j=-N..N [2N+1]. 2) terminal payoff. 3) roll back V=max(K-S, e^{-r dt}(pu V_up+pm V_mid+pd V_dn)). 4) European by same lattice without max. 5) check probabilities in [0,1]. 6) premium, write.
pitfalls: negative pm for large b dt: refine N

title: Leisen-Reimer tree for American option
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, q, sigma, N odd. DITANYAKAN: American price by Leisen-Reimer, compared with CRR. RUMUS: bsm card Core 7: h(z)=0.5+sign(z)sqrt(0.25-0.25 exp(-(z/(N+1/3+0.1/(N+1)))^2 (N+1/6))); p=h(d2), p'=h(d1), u=e^{(r-q)dt}p'/p, d=(e^{(r-q)dt}-p u)/(1-p); then V=max(payoff, continuation). JAWAB: 1) force N odd (N+1 if even, say so). 2) d1, d2 from BS with K. 3) build u, d, p. 4) roll back with exercise test. 5) CRR at same N (crr_price). 6) report both and difference. 7) write.
pitfalls: LR centres on strike K; with even N the inversion formula is off

title: Jarrow-Rudd equal-probability tree, American
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, q, sigma, N, type. DITANYAKAN: American price under Jarrow-Rudd tree (vs CRR). RUMUS: card V1(b): u,d = exp((r-q-sigma^2/2)dt +/- sigma sqrt dt), p=0.5, discount e^{-r dt}; V=max(payoff, continuation). JAWAB: 1) dt=T/N. 2) build u, d (tree recombines since u d is constant). 3) terminal payoff. 4) roll back with p=0.5 and early exercise. 5) price by CRR (crr_price) for comparison. 6) write both.
formulas: u, d = exp((r - q - sigma^2/2)dt +/- sigma sqrt dt)
pitfalls: JR is risk-neutral only in the limit; small N gives a drift bias

title: Early exercise boundary from a binomial tree
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, q, sigma, N. DITANYAKAN: put exercise boundary S*(t_n) at each step [N+1]. RUMUS: at step n the boundary is the largest node S with exercise value K-S >= continuation and K-S>0 (card conventions); at expiry S*(T)=K min(1, r/q). JAWAB: 1) roll back CRR, store per step a boolean exercise mask. 2) per n take max S_node with mask true, else 0.0. 3) set t_N value by the expiry rule. 4) check S*(t) < K and increasing toward T. 5) write [N+1] table.
formulas: S*(t_n) = max{S_j : K - S_j >= cont_j, K - S_j > 0}
pitfalls: tree boundary is a staircase; smooth or interpolate only if asked

title: Barone-Adesi-Whaley American call with dividend yield
deliverables: per contract [M]: baw_price, european_price, premium, critical_price S*
frame: DIKETAHUI: [M] S, K, T, r, q, sigma; b=r-q. DITANYAKAN: BAW call price, critical price S*, premium. RUMUS: card Core 3: M=2r/sigma^2, N=2b/sigma^2, K(T)=1-e^{-rT}, q2=[-(N-1)+sqrt((N-1)^2+4M/K)]/2; solve S*-X=c(S*)+[1-e^{(b-r)T}N(d1(S*))]S*/q2 by Brent on [X, 2X doubling]; A2=(S*/q2)[1-e^{(b-r)T}N(d1(S*))]; C=c(S)+A2(S/S*)^{q2} if S<S*, else S-X; toolkit baw_american. JAWAB: 1) if q<=0 return European, S*=inf/NaN. 2) solve S*. 3) A2. 4) price. 5) premium. 6) check C>=max(c, S-X). 7) write.
pitfalls: K(T) uses r, N uses b, M uses r

title: Barone-Adesi-Whaley American put and critical price S**
deliverables: per contract [M]: baw_put, european_put, premium, critical_price
frame: DIKETAHUI: [M] S, K, T, r, q, sigma. DITANYAKAN: BAW put price, S**, premium. RUMUS: card Core 3: q1=[-(N-1)-sqrt((N-1)^2+4M/K)]/2 (<0); solve X-S**=p(S**)-[1-e^{(b-r)T}N(-d1(S**))]S**/q1 by Brent on [X/2 halving, X]; A1=-(S**/q1)[1-e^{(b-r)T}N(-d1(S**))]; P=p(S)+A1(S/S**)^{q1} if S>S**, else X-S; toolkit baw_american(kind='put'). JAWAB: 1) inputs. 2) bracket and solve S**. 3) A1 > 0. 4) price per contract. 5) premium. 6) check S**<X, P>=X-S. 7) write.
pitfalls: sign of A1: negative q1 makes -S**/q1 positive

title: BAW for American options on futures (b = 0)
deliverables: per contract [M]: price, black76_price, premium, critical futures price
frame: DIKETAHUI: futures price F, K, T, r, sigma; b=0. DITANYAKAN: American call/put on futures, critical F*, premium vs Black-76. RUMUS: card Core 3 with b=0 so N=0, e^{(b-r)T}=e^{-rT}; European leg black76_price; both call and put have early exercise value when r>0. JAWAB: 1) set S=F, q=r (b=0). 2) solve critical price. 3) price via BAW (baw_american(q=r)). 4) European by black76_price. 5) premium > 0 for calls too. 6) write.
pitfalls: using e^{-qT} with q=0 instead of e^{-rT}: card pitfall for futures

title: American FX option by BAW (Garman-Kohlhagen carry)
deliverables: per contract [M]: american_price, gk_price, premium, critical_spot
frame: DIKETAHUI: spot S (domestic per foreign), K, T, r_d, r_f, sigma. DITANYAKAN: American FX call/put, premium vs European. RUMUS: b=r_d-r_f, q=r_f; BAW card Core 3; European toolkit garman_kohlhagen_price (or bs_price q=r_f); American baw_american(q=r_f). JAWAB: 1) map r=r_d, q=r_f. 2) European GK. 3) BAW price and critical spot. 4) premium. 5) check call premium > 0 iff r_f > 0, put premium > 0 iff r_d > 0. 6) write.
formulas: C_eu = S e^{-r_f T} N(d1) - K e^{-r_d T} N(d2)
pitfalls: swapping r_d and r_f flips which side has early exercise value

title: Bjerksund-Stensland 1993 American call
deliverables: per contract [M]: bs93_price, trigger I, european_price
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, X, T, r, b=r-q, sigma per contract [M]. DITANYAKAN: BS1993 American call and flat trigger I. RUMUS: card Core 4: beta=(1/2-b/sigma^2)+sqrt((b/sigma^2-1/2)^2+2r/sigma^2); B_inf=beta X/(beta-1); B0=max(X, rX/(r-b)); h=-(bT+2sigma sqrt T)B0/(B_inf-B0); I=B0+(B_inf-B0)(1-e^h); alpha=(I-X)I^{-beta}; C=alpha S^beta - alpha phi(S,T,beta,I,I)+phi(S,T,1,I,I)-phi(S,T,1,X,I)-X phi(S,T,0,I,I)+X phi(S,T,0,X,I). JAWAB: 1) if b>=r return European. 2) compute I. 3) if S>=I value S-X. 4) else formula with phi. 5) check >= European. 6) write.
formulas: phi = e^{lam T} S^g [N(d) - (I/S)^kap N(d - 2 ln(I/S)/(sigma sqrt T))]
pitfalls: B0 = max(X, rX/(r-b)) divides by zero when b = r; that case is European

title: Bjerksund-Stensland put via put-call transformation
deliverables: per contract [M]: put_price via transformed call
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, X, T, r, q, sigma. DITANYAKAN: American put by BS1993. RUMUS: card Core 4 transformation P(S,X,T,r,b,sigma)=C(X,S,T,r-b,-b,sigma) with C the BS1993 call. JAWAB: 1) b=r-q. 2) call inputs: spot'=X, strike'=S, r'=r-b=q, b'=-b. 3) evaluate BS1993 call with those (its own European short-circuit if b'>=r'). 4) result is the put. 5) check P>=max(X-S, European put). 6) write.
formulas: P(S, X, T, r, b, sigma) = C(X, S, T, r - b, -b, sigma)
pitfalls: swapping only S and X without changing r and b

title: Bjerksund-Stensland 2002 two-step boundary
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, X, T, r, q, sigma. DITANYAKAN: BS2002 price (more accurate than 1993) and comparison. RUMUS: card V4(c): split [0,T] at t1=0.5(sqrt5-1)T; triggers I1 (for T-t1) and I2 (for T) from the 1993 formula with h(t); price uses phi and the bivariate psi function (Haug 2007 ch.3) with bivariate_normal_cdf. JAWAB: 1) only if BS2002 named. 2) compute t1, I1, I2. 3) evaluate alpha1, alpha2. 4) assemble price with phi/psi terms. 5) compare with 1993 (2002 >= 1993 typically). 6) put by transformation. 7) write.
formulas: psi uses bivariate normal M(a, b; rho)
pitfalls: use only when the task names the 2002 version (card V4)

title: Compare BAW, Bjerksund-Stensland and CRR benchmark
deliverables: per contract [M]: baw, bs93, crr, rel_diff_baw, rel_diff_bs93
frame: DIKETAHUI: [M] contracts S, K, T, r, q, sigma, type; benchmark steps N (e.g. large). DITANYAKAN: price by each method, relative difference to the tree benchmark [M], summary max/mean abs rel diff. RUMUS: baw_american, BS1993 (card Core 4), crr_price(steps=N, averaged N,N+1); rel = (approx - bench)/bench. JAWAB: 1) inputs. 2) benchmark tree [M]. 3) BAW [M]. 4) BS93 [M]. 5) rel diffs [M]. 6) summary. 7) check diffs small and larger for long T; write.
pitfalls: benchmark with odd/even oscillation biases the ranking; average N and N+1

title: Perpetual American put
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, X, r, q, sigma (no T). DITANYAKAN: perpetual American put value and exercise level. RUMUS: card Core 5: M=2r/sigma^2, N=2(r-q)/sigma^2, g=[-(N-1)-sqrt((N-1)^2+4M)]/2 <0; S*=X g/(g-1); V=(X-S*)(S/S*)^g for S>S*, else X-S. JAWAB: 1) compute g. 2) S*. 3) value by region. 4) check S*<X, V>=X-S, V smooth-pasting slope -1 at S*. 5) write.

title: Perpetual American call with dividend yield
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, X, r, q>0, sigma. DITANYAKAN: perpetual call value and S*. RUMUS: positive root h=[-(N-1)+sqrt((N-1)^2+4M)]/2 >1 (M=2r/sigma^2, N=2(r-q)/sigma^2); S*=X h/(h-1); V=(S*-X)(S/S*)^h for S<S*, else S-X. JAWAB: 1) require q>0 (else value=S, never exercised). 2) h. 3) S*. 4) value. 5) check S*>X, V>=S-X. 6) write.
pitfalls: with q = 0 there is no finite S*: value tends to S

title: Crank-Nicolson + PSOR American put on an S-grid
deliverables: scalar: price at S0; grid values [N_S+1]
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, K, T, r, q, sigma; N_S, N_t, Smax; omega, tol. DITANYAKAN: American put at S0 (and grid). RUMUS: card Core 2 + bsm Core 5: CN coefficients; A v = rhs with sub -alpha, diag 1-beta, super -gamma; PSOR y=(rhs_i+alpha_i v_{i-1}+gamma_i v_{i+1})/(1-beta_i), v_i<-max(payoff_i, v_i+omega(y-v_i)), Gauss-Seidel order. JAWAB: 1) grid S_i=i dS, K on node. 2) v=payoff. 3) each step: rhs from explicit half; BC V(0)=K, V(Smax)=0. 4) PSOR until max|dv|<tol. 5) interpolate at S0. 6) check V>=payoff. 7) write.
formulas: y = (rhs_i + alpha_i v_{i-1} + gamma_i v_{i+1})/(1 - beta_i)
pitfalls: pure Python PSOR loops are slow: cap iterations or vectorise where possible

title: Exercise boundary from PSOR grid per time layer
frame: DIKETAHUI: PDE setup as CN+PSOR, tolerance eps for contact. DITANYAKAN: S*(t) per layer [N_t+1]. RUMUS: card conventions: S* = largest S_i with |V_i - payoff_i| < eps and payoff_i>0 (scan high S downward); 0.0 if none; at expiry S*=K min(1, r/q). JAWAB: 1) solve CN+PSOR storing each layer. 2) per layer scan from high S down for contact. 3) cap at K. 4) check boundary < K, decreasing as tau grows. 5) write [N_t+1].
formulas: S*(t) = max{S_i : |V_i - (K - S_i)| < eps, K - S_i > 0}
pitfalls: eps 1e-10 gives spurious zeros; too loose drifts above K - cap at K

title: Brennan-Schwartz direct solve for American put
deliverables: scalar price; optional comparison with PSOR
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, K, T, r, q, sigma, grid sizes. DITANYAKAN: American put by Brennan-Schwartz (exact for vanilla put). RUMUS: card Core 2 alternative: solve CN tridiagonal with Gaussian elimination running from high S to low S (upper-to-lower sweep), projecting v_i=max(v_i, payoff_i) during back substitution starting at S=0 side. JAWAB: 1) build CN system. 2) eliminate in reverse order so substitution proceeds from S=0 upward. 3) project during substitution. 4) step N_t layers. 5) compare with PSOR price. 6) write.
formulas: v_i = max(payoff_i, (d_i - c_i v_{i+1})/b_i) in back substitution
pitfalls: wrong sweep direction makes the projection inexact for puts

title: Penalty method for American option PDE
frame: DIKETAHUI: PDE setup, penalty factor rho_pen (large), tol. DITANYAKAN: American price by penalty iteration. RUMUS: add rho_pen max(payoff - V, 0) to the discrete system (Forsyth-Vetzal); per step iterate: solve (A + P^k) v^{k+1} = rhs + P^k payoff, P^k = diag(rho_pen if v^k < payoff else 0), until active set unchanged. JAWAB: 1) build CN matrix. 2) per step iterate active set. 3) stop when set stable or max|dv|<tol. 4) price at S0. 5) compare with PSOR. 6) write.

title: Explicit finite difference with max projection
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, K, T, r, q, sigma, N_S, N_t. DITANYAKAN: American put by explicit FD with projection. RUMUS: card V6(c), bsm Core 5: V^n_i = a V^{n+1}_{i-1}+(1+b)V^{n+1}_i+c V^{n+1}_{i+1}, then V^n_i=max(V^n_i, payoff_i); stable if dt <= 1/(sigma^2 N_S^2) roughly. JAWAB: 1) check stability; if violated increase N_t and say so. 2) step backward with projection each layer. 3) BC. 4) interpolate S0. 5) check V>=payoff. 6) write.
formulas: V^n_i = max(payoff_i, a V_{i-1} + (1+b) V_i + c V_{i+1})
pitfalls: unstable dt gives exploding oscillations, not a small error

title: Fully implicit scheme + PSOR
frame: DIKETAHUI: PDE setup. DITANYAKAN: American put with implicit time stepping (O(dt)). RUMUS: card V6(b): (I - L dt) v^n = v^{n+1}, solved by PSOR with projection; unconditionally stable, no CN kink oscillation. JAWAB: 1) build implicit matrix diag 1-b_i, off -a_i, -c_i. 2) PSOR per step. 3) price at S0. 4) compare with CN+PSOR; difference ~ O(dt). 5) write.

title: Richardson extrapolation on a PDE grid (halve dS and dt)
frame: DIKETAHUI: PDE solver, coarse grid (N_S, N_t), fine grid (2N_S, 2N_t). DITANYAKAN: extrapolated price and convergence ratio. RUMUS: card Core 6: P=(4P_fine-P_coarse)/3; ratio |P_c-P_rich|/|P_f-P_rich| ~ 4. JAWAB: 1) solve coarse. 2) solve fine with BOTH dS and dt halved, S0 and K on nodes. 3) Richardson. 4) ratio. 5) report (American kink reduces order; ratio may be <4). 6) write.
pitfalls: halving only dS or only dt invalidates the 4:1 weights

title: Discrete cash dividend in a binomial tree (escrowed model)
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, sigma, dividends D_j at t_j [D], N. DITANYAKAN: American call/put with cash dividends. RUMUS: card V5(b) Hull: S*=S-sum D_j e^{-r t_j}; tree on S*; at node time t, node stock = S*_node + sum_{t_j>t} D_j e^{-r(t_j-t)}; exercise against that stock. European: bs_price(S*). JAWAB: 1) PV of dividends before T. 2) tree on S*. 3) at each node add back PV of remaining dividends. 4) roll back with max. 5) European. 6) premium; write.
formulas: S* = S - sum D_j e^{-r t_j}
pitfalls: sigma here applies to S*, not S; say which if the task is silent

title: Discrete cash dividend in a PDE: jump condition
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, K, T, r, sigma, dividend D at t_d (or several), PDE grid. DITANYAKAN: American price with jump. RUMUS: card V5(a): stepping backward, at step index round(t_d/dt): V(S, t_d-) = V(max(S-D,0), t_d+) by linear interpolation on grid, then re-apply max(V, payoff). JAWAB: 1) locate dividend step. 2) step CN+PSOR backward. 3) at the dividend layer apply the jump. 4) re-project. 5) continue to t=0. 6) price at S0; check puts rise vs no-dividend. 7) write.
formulas: V <- max(V, payoff) after the jump
pitfalls: S + D instead of S - D, or forgetting to re-project after the jump

title: Optimal exercise just before ex-dividend date (call)
frame: DIKETAHUI: K, r, T, dividend dates t_1..t_n and amounts D_i. DITANYAKAN: whether early exercise just before each ex-date can be optimal. RUMUS: Hull: exercise before t_i never optimal if D_i <= K(1 - e^{-r(t_{i+1}-t_i)}) (t_{n+1}=T). JAWAB: 1) sort dividends. 2) per i compute threshold K(1-e^{-r(t_{i+1}-t_i)}). 3) flag D_i > threshold. 4) if no flag, American call = European on S - PV(D). 5) write per-dividend table.
formulas: D_i <= K (1 - e^{-r (t_{i+1} - t_i)}) => no exercise at t_i

title: Black's approximation for American call with dividends
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, sigma, dividends D_i at t_i. DITANYAKAN: Black pseudo-American call. RUMUS: Hull: value = max(c_T, c_{t_n}), c_T European to T on S - PV(all D); c_{t_n} European expiring just before last ex-date on S - PV(D before t_n); bs_price. JAWAB: 1) PV dividends. 2) European to T. 3) European to t_n (exclude D_n). 4) max. 5) write the three numbers.
formulas: C_black = max(c(S - PV_T(D), T), c(S - PV_{t_n}(D), t_n))
pitfalls: the t_n option excludes the dividend paid at t_n itself

title: Bermudan option on stated exercise dates via tree
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, q, sigma, exercise dates t_e [E], N. DITANYAKAN: Bermudan price, between European and American. RUMUS: card V3(b): roll back CRR; apply max(payoff, continuation) only at steps n = round(t_e/dt); elsewhere continuation only. JAWAB: 1) map dates to steps (align N so dates fall on nodes). 2) roll back with conditional exercise. 3) European and American with same N. 4) check E <= B <= A. 5) write.
formulas: V_n = max(payoff, cont) if n in exercise steps else cont
pitfalls: rounding dates to steps silently: report the mapping

title: Bermudan option by PDE with exercise only on dates
frame: DIKETAHUI: PDE setup, exercise dates [E]. DITANYAKAN: Bermudan price. RUMUS: CN European steps (Thomas, no PSOR) between dates; at each exercise layer V=max(V, payoff). JAWAB: 1) choose N_t so dates hit layers. 2) Thomas solve per step. 3) project at date layers. 4) price at S0. 5) check between European and American. 6) write.

title: American put-call parity bounds check
deliverables: per pair [P]: C - P, lower, upper, within flag
frame: DIKETAHUI: American call and put prices at same K, T; S, r, q. DITANYAKAN: whether C-P lies within American parity bounds. RUMUS: card: S e^{-qT} - K <= C - P <= S - K e^{-rT} (q=0: S - K <= C - P <= S - K e^{-rT}). JAWAB: 1) pair calls and puts. 2) compute bounds. 3) flag inside/outside with tolerance. 4) amount of violation. 5) counts; write.
formulas: S e^{-qT} - K <= C - P <= S - K e^{-rT}
pitfalls: applying European equality to American prices

title: Early exercise premium across moneyness
deliverables: table [G]: S, american, european, premium, exercised flag
frame: DIKETAHUI: K, T, r, q, sigma, spot grid [G]. DITANYAKAN: premium vs S. RUMUS: American by crr_price or baw_american, European by bs_price; premium = A - E; if S <= S** then A = K - S. JAWAB: 1) grid. 2) A and E per S. 3) premium. 4) flag immediate exercise region. 5) check premium peaks near S** and A >= intrinsic. 6) write table.

title: Call early exercise premium vs dividend yield
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, sigma, q grid [Q]. DITANYAKAN: American call premium as q varies. RUMUS: baw_american or crr_price per q; premium = A - E; zero at q=0. JAWAB: 1) loop q. 2) prices. 3) premium. 4) check monotone increasing in q. 5) write.

title: Exercise boundary at expiry and near-expiry limit
deliverables: scalar: S*(T) for put and call
frame: DIKETAHUI: K, r, q. DITANYAKAN: boundary value at expiry. RUMUS: card conventions: put S*(T)=K min(1, r/q) (=K when q=0); call S*(T)=K max(1, r/q) (infinite when q=0). JAWAB: 1) compute both. 2) use as terminal boundary in boundary arrays. 3) write.

title: American Greeks from the binomial tree
deliverables: scalar or [M]: price, delta, gamma, theta (per year/day)
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, q, sigma, N. DITANYAKAN: American delta, gamma, theta. RUMUS: Hull: delta=(V_u-V_d)/(S u-S d) at step1; gamma=[(V_uu-V_ud)/(S_uu-S_ud)-(V_ud-V_dd)/(S_ud-S_dd)]/(0.5(S_uu-S_dd)) at step2; theta=(V_ud-V_0)/(2dt) per year. JAWAB: 1) roll back storing steps 1-2. 2) delta, gamma, theta. 3) convert theta /365 if per day. 4) check put delta in [-1,0]. 5) write.
pitfalls: theta unit: per year by default, /365 only if per calendar day

title: American Greeks from PDE grid
deliverables: scalar: price, delta, gamma, theta, vega (bump)
frame: DIKETAHUI: CN+PSOR grid solution. DITANYAKAN: Greeks at S0. RUMUS: bsm card conventions: delta=(V_{i+1}-V_{i-1})/(2dS), gamma=(V_{i+1}-2V_i+V_{i-1})/dS^2, theta from layers t=0 and t=dt; vega by re-solving with sigma +/- h on same grid. JAWAB: 1) solve. 2) central differences at S0 node. 3) theta. 4) vega bump. 5) check delta=-1 inside exercise region. 6) write.

title: Delta and gamma inside the exercise region
deliverables: grid table [G]: S, V, delta, in_exercise
frame: DIKETAHUI: American put values on spot grid [G] and boundary S**. DITANYAKAN: verify delta = -1 and gamma = 0 for S < S**, smooth pasting at S**. RUMUS: V = K - S below S**; dV/dS continuous at S** (smooth pasting). JAWAB: 1) compute grid delta. 2) mask S < S**. 3) max|delta+1| in mask. 4) slope jump across S**. 5) write table and flags.
formulas: V = K - S, Delta = -1 for S < S**

title: CRR convergence table over step counts
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, q, sigma, list of N [K], reference (or largest N). DITANYAKAN: price per N and error. RUMUS: crr_price(steps=N); error = P_N - P_ref; optional averaged column. JAWAB: 1) loop N. 2) prices. 3) reference. 4) errors. 5) check |error| decreasing ~1/N with oscillation. 6) write.

title: Implied volatility from an American option price
frame: DIKETAHUI: American market price V, S, K, T, r, q, type. DITANYAKAN: sigma such that model price = V. RUMUS: brentq on f(sigma)=model(sigma)-V on [1e-4, 5], model = baw_american or crr_price (fixed N, averaged); NaN if V < intrinsic. JAWAB: 1) check V >= intrinsic. 2) bracket. 3) solve tol 1e-8. 4) reprice check. 5) write.
pitfalls: using European implied_vol on an American price overstates put IV

title: Longstaff-Schwartz least squares Monte Carlo American put
deliverables: scalar: lsm_price, standard_error; compare to tree
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, q, sigma, n_paths, n_steps, seed, basis (1, S, S^2 or Laguerre). DITANYAKAN: LSM price and SE. RUMUS: Glasserman: simulate GBM [N x T]; backward: at each date regress discounted future cashflow on basis over ITM paths; exercise if K-S > fitted continuation; price = mean discounted cashflow. JAWAB: 1) paths (gbm_paths). 2) cashflow = payoff at T. 3) loop back regress ITM only. 4) update exercise. 5) price, SE=std/sqrt(N). 6) compare with crr_price. 7) write.
formulas: cont(S) = beta0 + beta1 S + beta2 S^2
pitfalls: regressing on all paths (not ITM only) biases the boundary

title: BAW critical price iteration with Haug seed
frame: DIKETAHUI: X, T, r, b, sigma, tolerance. DITANYAKAN: BAW critical price by Newton with seed. RUMUS: Haug: seed from T->inf: q2_inf=[-(N-1)+sqrt((N-1)^2+4M)]/2, S_inf=X/(1-1/q2_inf), h2=-(bT+2sigma sqrt T)X/(S_inf-X), S_seed=X+(S_inf-X)(1-e^{h2}); Newton on LHS-RHS of card Core 3 equation. JAWAB: 1) seed. 2) iterate until |LHS-RHS|/X < tol. 3) fallback Brent. 4) report S* and iterations; write.

title: Missing dividend yield from forward, then American price
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, forward F (or futures) to T, r, K, sigma. DITANYAKAN: q then American price. RUMUS: q = r - ln(F/S)/T; then baw_american(q=q) or crr_price(q=q). JAWAB: 1) q from forward. 2) price. 3) report q and price. 4) write.

title: American option on futures by binomial tree
frame: DIKETAHUI: futures F, K, T, r, sigma, N. DITANYAKAN: American futures option by tree. RUMUS: Hull: futures tree p=(1-d)/(u-d) (q=r), discount e^{-r dt}; toolkit crr_price(S=F, q=r); European black76_price. JAWAB: 1) build tree on F. 2) roll back with max(payoff). 3) European. 4) premium. 5) write.

title: American FX option by binomial tree
frame: DIKETAHUI: spot S, K, T, r_d, r_f, sigma, N. DITANYAKAN: American FX option by tree vs GK European. RUMUS: p=(e^{(r_d-r_f)dt}-d)/(u-d), discount r_d; crr_price(r=r_d, q=r_f); garman_kohlhagen_price. JAWAB: 1) map rates. 2) tree. 3) European. 4) premium. 5) write.

title: Deep ITM put: immediate exercise
deliverables: per contract [M]: price, exercise_now flag, premium
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, q, sigma, S** (or computed). DITANYAKAN: value and premium when S <= S**. RUMUS: card: value = K - S (intrinsic), premium = (K - S) - p_eu. JAWAB: 1) compute S** (baw_american / tree boundary). 2) flag S <= S**. 3) value = intrinsic for flagged. 4) premium. 5) check premium >= 0. 6) write.
formulas: P_am = K - S for S <= S**

title: Critical price term structure across maturities
frame: DIKETAHUI: K, r, q, sigma, maturities [T]. DITANYAKAN: S** and S* per maturity. RUMUS: BAW critical-price equations (card Core 3); perpetual limit card Core 5. JAWAB: 1) loop T. 2) solve put and call critical prices. 3) perpetual limits. 4) check put S** decreasing in T toward perpetual, call S* increasing. 5) write.

title: Trinomial vs binomial price comparison
frame: DIKETAHUI: contract inputs, list N [K]. DITANYAKAN: both lattice prices per N. RUMUS: card Core 1 CRR and Boyle. JAWAB: 1) loop N. 2) crr_price. 3) trinomial. 4) differences; trinomial smoother. 5) write.

title: Log-price grid for American put PDE
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, K, T, r, q, sigma, x-range, N_x, N_t. DITANYAKAN: American put on x=ln S grid. RUMUS: bsm card Core 6: V_t+(r-q-sigma^2/2)V_x+0.5sigma^2V_xx-rV=0; CN + PSOR with payoff K-e^x; BC V(x_min)=K e^{-r tau}-e^{x_min}e^{-q tau} or K-e^{x_min}, V(x_max)=0. JAWAB: 1) grid centred at ln S0 with ln K on node. 2) coefficients. 3) CN+PSOR. 4) read V at x0. 5) write.
formulas: V_t + (r - q - sigma^2/2) V_x + 0.5 sigma^2 V_xx - r V = 0

title: Exercise-now decision table for a portfolio
deliverables: per contract [M]: S, S_crit, exercise_now, value, intrinsic
frame: DIKETAHUI: [M] American positions S, K, T, r, q, sigma, type. DITANYAKAN: whether to exercise today per contract. RUMUS: exercise if intrinsic >= continuation, equivalently put S <= S**, call S >= S* (baw_american critical or tree at t=0). JAWAB: 1) per contract value and intrinsic. 2) critical price. 3) flag. 4) counts. 5) write.

title: Batch American pricing with input validation
deliverables: per contract [M]: id, method, price, european, premium; summary counts
frame: DIKETAHUI: table [M] with mixed types, rates maybe in percent, method column. DITANYAKAN: American price per row by named method, summary. RUMUS: card worked frame; crr_price, baw_american, bs_price. JAWAB: 1) validate ids unique, percent -> decimal (values > 1). 2) dispatch method per row. 3) European. 4) premium. 5) invariants per row (A>=E>=0, A>=intrinsic). 6) summary counts and violations. 7) round last; write.
pitfalls: writing the pandas index or reordering rows

title: Early exercise premium decomposition (integral representation)
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, K, T, r, q, sigma, boundary S*(t) on [0,T] grid. DITANYAKAN: American put = European + EEP integral. RUMUS: Kim (1990): EEP = int_0^T [rK e^{-r u} N(-d2(S, S*(t+u), u)) - qS e^{-q u} N(-d1(S, S*(t+u), u))] du. JAWAB: 1) boundary from PSOR/tree. 2) quadrature over u (trapezoid). 3) add European. 4) compare with grid price. 5) write.
formulas: EEP = int_0^T [rK e^{-ru} N(-d2) - qS e^{-qu} N(-d1)] du

title: Smax and grid placement for American PDE
frame: DIKETAHUI: S0, K, T, sigma, N_S. DITANYAKAN: price with sensible far boundary and S0/K on nodes. RUMUS: bsm card: Smax 3-5K or K exp(5 sigma sqrt T); put BC V(0)=K, V(Smax)=0; dS = Smax/N_S chosen so K/dS integer. JAWAB: 1) choose Smax. 2) adjust N_S so K and S0 on nodes (or interpolate cubic). 3) solve. 4) sensitivity to Smax doubling < tol. 5) write.
formulas: Smax = K exp(5 sigma sqrt T)

title: PSOR omega and tolerance diagnostics
frame: DIKETAHUI: PDE setup, omega grid [W] in (1,2), tol. DITANYAKAN: iterations and price per omega. RUMUS: card Core 2: stop when max|dv|<tol; omega 1.2-1.5 typical. JAWAB: 1) loop omega. 2) solve counting iterations. 3) prices agree within tol. 4) pick minimum iterations. 5) write.
